exhilarated

ig-ZIL-uh-ray-tid · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Exhilarated is feeling very happy, animated, or elated.

She felt utterly exhilarated after crossing the finish line of her first marathon.

Example

The hikers looked exhilarated as they finally reached the peak at sunrise.

Exhilarated describes a temporary, intense burst of happy energy right after a specific thrilling event, not an ongoing personality trait.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

thrilled: Thrilled means feeling great excitement or delight — a leaping, can't-wait-to-tell-someone reaction to good news. Exhilarated adds a physical charge on top: a rush of happy, animated energy right after one specific event, the feeling of adrenaline still fizzing through your body.

energized: Energized means given new energy or vigor, ready to get back to work — and anything can do it: a nap, a coffee, a pep talk. Exhilarated is that energy wrapped in intense happiness, the joyful rush right after something thrilling has just happened.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

deflated: having lost enthusiasm or confidence

dejected: sad and depressed

Where it sits · how intense the happiness gets

pleased → exhilarated → overjoyed

pleased vs. exhilarated: Being pleased is a mild, quiet satisfaction; being exhilarated is a full-body rush of happy energy.

overjoyed vs. exhilarated: Overjoyed pushes past exhilarated into an almost overwhelming flood of happiness.

Which word fits?

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ex-: thoroughly, out (Latin)

root — hilar: cheerful (Latin (hilaris))

suffix — -ated: adjective-forming, past-participle ending (Latin)

Put it together: ex- ("thoroughly") + hilar ("cheerful") + -ated (adjective ending) = made thoroughly cheerful.

Use the root in a new word: hilarious: The hilarity at the lunch table stopped the moment the principal walked in.
